info.name: SmartShelf ESL API (Minew)
info.description:
Product and ESL integration API for SmartShelf.

## Getting started
1. Select the **SmartShelf ESL** environment and set `baseUrl`, `userName`, `password`.
2. Run **Auth > Login**. The token is captured into `{{token}}` automatically and every other request uses it.
3. Set `storeId` in the environment - every product operation is scoped to one store.

## Notes
- All prices reach the ESL labels as part of the create/update call. There is **no separate push or sync endpoint to fire**.
- A label only repaints if it is bound to the product with a template, and the store must have a `MinewStoreId`.
- **Scheduling** times are UTC (Sri Lanka is UTC+5:30). The create requests fill them in for you.
- Bulk endpoints are **partial-success**: a bad row is reported with a reason and the rest of the batch still lands. Check `result.results[]` per row, not just the HTTP status.

request.description:
Logs in with the employee ID and password. Saves `token`, `storeId` and `userId` into the environment for every other request in this collection.

`userName` is the **Employee ID**, not the email address.

request.description: Category ids and names for the store. Bulk payloads may reference a category either by `categoryId` or by `categoryName`.
All active ESL devices. Use the `id` values here as `deviceId` inside `eslAssignments`.

Minew label templates synced into SmartShelf. Use the `id` values here as `templateId` inside `eslAssignments`.

request.description:
Creates the product **and** its label bindings in one database transaction - if any binding is invalid nothing is saved, so a product can never end up half-configured.

The price is pushed to the label as part of this call.

`eslAssignments` is optional; send `[]` to create without a label.

Get `deviceId` from **Reference data > Devices**, `templateId` from **Reference data > Templates**.

**The template must belong to the same Minew store as the device, and match its screen size.** A template id from another store is accepted locally and then rejected by the cloud with `模板不存在` ("template does not exist"). Pull the id from **Reference data > Templates** and check its `storeId` and `screenInch` against the device.

**This one call now puts the product on the label.** The ESL assignment is saved *and* bound in the vendor cloud, so the label starts displaying immediately - there is no separate bind call. Set `"bindToEsl": false` to record the assignment locally only.

The response message reports the outcome, e.g. `"...created successfully. 1 label(s) bound."`

Updates the product and reconciles its label bindings in one transaction.

To **remove** an existing binding, send that row with `"isDeleted": true` and its saved `templateAssignmentId` / `messageAssignmentId` (both come back from the lookup endpoints).

**The template must belong to the same Minew store as the device, and match its screen size.** A template id from another store is accepted locally and then rejected by the cloud with `模板不存在` ("template does not exist"). Pull the id from **Reference data > Templates** and check its `storeId` and `screenInch` against the device.

**This one call now puts the product on the label.** The ESL assignment is saved *and* bound in the vendor cloud, so the label starts displaying immediately - there is no separate bind call. Set `"bindToEsl": false` to record the assignment locally only.

The response message reports the outcome, e.g. `"...created successfully. 1 label(s) bound."`

Paged product list for one store. Returns product fields only (no ESL data) - it is the grid/list feed.

For ESL data use **Get product by code** or **Get product details by id**.

Returns HTTP 404 with `totalCount: 0` when nothing matches.

item.name: Get product by CODE (with ESL data)

request.description:
**Whole product record for a product code, including every ESL bound to it.**

`storeId` is required - product codes are unique per store, not globally.

Response highlights:
- `hasEsl` - true when at least one label is bound, so you can branch without inspecting the array
- `eslDevices[]` - one entry per label, with `deviceId`, `mac`, `templateId`/`templateName`, `messageId`/`messageName`, battery and online state

A label bound with both a template and a message appears **once** with both sets of fields populated.

Returns 404 when the code does not exist in that store.

item.name: Get product details by id (with ESL data)

request.description: Identical payload to **Get product by code**, keyed on the internal product id.

request.description:
Creates many products from one JSON payload, optionally with their ESL bindings, and pushes the prices to the labels in the same call.

**Category may be given by id or by name.** `categoryName` exists so an external POS/ERP does not need to know SmartShelf's internal ids. `categoryId` wins if both are sent.

**Partial success.** HTTP is 200 even when some rows fail. Read `result.results[]`:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `index` | position in the payload you sent |
| `success` | did the row save |
| `productId` | new id when it did |
| `message` | reason when it did not |
| `eslPushed` | `true`/`false`, or `null` when no push was attempted |
| `eslMessage` | what the label push returned |

Set `"pushToEsl": false` for a data-only load (migration, seeding) with no cloud traffic.

A failing row rolls back only itself.

**The template must belong to the same Minew store as the device, and match its screen size.** A template id from another store is accepted locally and then rejected by the cloud with `模板不存在` ("template does not exist"). Pull the id from **Reference data > Templates** and check its `storeId` and `screenInch` against the device.

exec: r.results.filter(x => x.eslPushed === false).forEach(x => console.log(`ESL not pushed for ${x.productCode}: ${x.eslMessage}`));

request.description:
**The price-feed endpoint.** Updates many products from one JSON payload and pushes every new price to its label in the same call - there is no second endpoint to fire.

**Rows are matched on `productCode` within `storeId`.** Send `id` instead if you prefer to match on the internal id.

**Only the fields you send are changed.** Every field is optional, so a price-only feed like the example will not blank descriptions, barcodes or categories. This is the difference from `PUT /api/products/product/{id}`, which replaces the whole record.

Partial success, same `result.results[]` shape as bulk create. `result.eslSummary` gives the one-line outcome.

**When a price will not reach a label:**
1. the store has no `MinewStoreId` - reported as `"Store has no MinewStoreId - saved to database only."`
2. no label is bound to that product with a template - the push succeeds but nothing repaints

item.name: Scheduling (queues)
item.description:
Scheduled label updates. A queue is a device + a template + a product, with a start and end time.

**The price is read when the queue fires, not when you create it.** Schedule a promo window today and the label picks up whatever the selling price is at that moment - you do not bake the price into the schedule.

**Times are UTC.** The processor compares against `DateTime.UtcNow`, so a 3:00pm Sri Lanka promo is `09:30` UTC. The two create requests below fill `startDate` / `endDate` automatically via a pre-request script, so they just work; copy that script if you build your own.

**Timing:** the processor polls every 30 seconds and activates at most 20 queues per cycle. Fine for promotions, not for second-accurate work.

request.description:
**The headline scheduling call.** Binds a product to a label at `startDate` and reverts at `endDate`.

`startDate` and `endDate` are filled in by the pre-request script as UTC, starting 2 minutes from now - run it, then watch the label change.

| Field | | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `deviceId` | required | From **Reference data > Devices** |
| `templateId` | required for Minew | Quoted string. Minew queues always need one, even when the point is the message |
| `messageId` | optional | Rides alongside the template; its image goes to the label |
| `locationType` | required | `PRODUCT` or `SHELF` |
| `locationId` | required | The product id when `locationType` is `PRODUCT` |
| `startDate` | required | **UTC**, `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss` |
| `endDate` | optional | Set it - the overlap check below cannot compare against an open-ended queue |
| `priorityId` | optional | See **Priority types**. Defaults to `4` (Scheduled); use `2` for a price change |
| `isRecurring` / `recurrencePattern` | optional | `DAILY`, `WEEKLY`, `MONTHLY`, `HOURLY` |

`storeId` is not sent - it is taken from the device.

Returns **409 Conflict** when an unfinished queue already targets the same device and template over an overlapping window.

**The template must belong to the same Minew store as the device, and match its screen size.** A template id from another store is accepted locally and then rejected by the cloud with `模板不存在` ("template does not exist"). Pull the id from **Reference data > Templates** and check its `storeId` and `screenInch` against the device.

exec: // The scheduler compares against DateTime.UtcNow, so startDate/endDate must be UTC.
// Sri Lanka is UTC+5:30 - a local 3:00pm promo is 09:30 UTC.
// These build a window starting 2 minutes from now so the sample fires while you watch.
console.log('That is', start.toLocaleString(), '->', end.toLocaleString(), 'in your local time.');

request.description:
Same endpoint, with recurrence. The queue re-arms after each run according to `recurrencePattern`.

Because the price is resolved at execution time, a daily recurring queue keeps showing the current price without being touched again.

`assignmentId` is the `templateAssignmentId` (or `messageAssignmentId`) returned by **Product lookup > Get product by code**.

request.description: Paged list with filters. `status` accepts the queue status names - `Pending`, `Processing`, `Completed`, `Failed`.

item.name: Get queue by id (with execution history)

request.description:
One queue, including what happened when it ran.

Every attempt writes a `QueueExecutionLog` row, pass or fail. When a label did not change, this is where the reason is: `errorMessage` carries Minew's own rejection text, and `bindingData` holds the raw cloud response.

A rejected bind is recorded as **Failed**, not silently completed - the code checks Minew's response body rather than trusting the HTTP status.

What is about to run. The best single check that a schedule was accepted and is armed.

Returns the queue with its resolved `locationName` / `productName`, so you can confirm the right product is attached without a second lookup.
Queues currently in their display window.
Everything scheduled against one label - useful when a label is showing something unexpected.

Moves the window or changes recurrence. Only the fields you send are applied - all of them are optional except `userId`.

Times are UTC, same as on create.

exec: // The scheduler compares against DateTime.UtcNow, so startDate/endDate must be UTC.
// Sri Lanka is UTC+5:30 - a local 3:00pm promo is 09:30 UTC.
// These build a window starting 2 minutes from now so the sample fires while you watch.
console.log('That is', start.toLocaleString(), '->', end.toLocaleString(), 'in your local time.');

request.description:
Fires the queue immediately instead of waiting for its start time - the fastest way to prove the whole chain works during a demo.

This performs the **real cloud bind**, so the physical label repaints.

Returns **400** if the start time has not arrived, and **409** if the queue has already run - most often because the background processor picked it up first. Neither changes the queue's recorded outcome.

Retires a running queue. It stays `Completed` rather than reverting to `Pending`, so the history stays truthful, and `isActive` is cleared so it no longer drives the label - which also makes it deletable.

Removes the schedule.

Returns **409** if the queue is still inside its display window and has not been deactivated - deactivate it first, then delete. A queue that has already finished, or been deactivated, deletes straight away.
Counts by status for a store - pending, completed, failed.

The `priorityId` values:

| Id | Code | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `EMERGENCY` | Price errors, out-of-stock |
| 2 | `PRICE_CHANGE` | Price updates and corrections |
| 3 | `PROMOTION` | Promotional content |
| 4 | `SCHEDULED` | Routine rotation (the default) |
| 5 | `MAINTENANCE` | Device health checks |

query.description: Optional - only needed if the same MAC is registered in more than one store

request.description:
**Whole device record for a MAC, including everything it is currently bound to.**

The MAC may be given bare (`e0000000be65`) or separated (`e0:00:00:00:be:65` / `e0-00-00-00-be-65`) - both match the same device, and case does not matter.

`storeId` is optional; supply it only to disambiguate a MAC registered in more than one store.

Response highlights:
- hardware state: `battery`, `isOnline`, `lastSeen`, `firmware`, screen size and colour
- `minewDeviceId` and `minewStoreId` - the cloud-side identifiers
- `isBound` / `bindings[]` - what the label is showing: `productCode`, `productName`, `sellingPrice`, `discountPrice`, `templateName`, `messageName`

Returns 404 when no device carries that MAC.
Device record by internal id. Returns the device fields only - use **by MAC** for the version that includes bindings.

Forces a label to re-render a product it is already assigned to.

You should not normally need this - creating or updating a product with ESL assignments binds the label automatically. Use it to repaint a label that was offline at bind time, or after changing a template outside the product flow.

`comboId` is the `deviceTemplateComboId` from **Get product by code**; `productId` is the product to render.

Roles: Admin or Manager only.
